architecture.mechanism: Deep-learning-based object detection for identifying structural defects and degradation in overhead panel mounting systems
architecture.intervention: Embed a miniature vision sensor in the overhead console housing to continuously monitor the headliner mounting interface using a trained convolutional neural network, triggering an audible alert and activating a secondary mechanical retention latch when spalling, cracks, or fastener loosening is detected before full detachment occurs
architecture.expected_effect: Early detection of mounting surface deterioration prevents complete console detachment under vehicle vibration and temperature cycling without altering the primary headliner material or interfering with dash camera wiring
architecture.falsification_test: Subject the instrumented console assembly to 500 hours of combined random vibration (10-500 Hz per ISO 16750-3) and thermal cycling (-40C to +85C) while artificially introducing progressive micro-cracks at the mounting points; verify that the CNN detects structural defects and triggers the secondary latch before detachment force threshold is reached, with zero damage to the headliner substrate
